result.judge_notes: pass 1 (A=without, B=with): Both answers commit to a 4px base, give spacing and type tables a developer could implement, and tie their reasoning to dense tables and gloved touch. B handles the desktop/tablet tension more cleanly with explicit density token pairs (row height, control height, minimum tap target, gap between targets) and a tablet type minimum. A instead scales the root font by about 1.14 on tablet, which pushes the scaled values off the 4px grid. A handles Dev C's Tailwind point a bit more fully, since it explains that Tailwind's type scale is hand-picked and so can't settle the ratio question. | pass 2 (A=with, B=without): Both answers pick a 4px base and give tokens a developer could implement. B handles Tailwind better: it explains that Tailwind's spacing is already 4px but its type scale is hand-picked, so Tailwind can't settle the type question. B also covers more contexts (compact desktop, default desktop, gloved tablet) and gives a clear trade-off. B's tablet trick of switching the root font size has a flaw: it would also scale rem-based spacing off the 4px grid. A is tighter but treats the Tailwind suggestion only in passing, and some of its type steps (19, 23, 33) are odd hand-set values.
